transcript:
[doctor] Hi Mr. Harris, how are you today?

[patient] Hi, doctor. I've been better. I've been having some trouble with my urinary habits.

[doctor] Hmm, I see. Can you tell me more about what's been going on?

[patient] Sure. For the past 6 months, I've been having difficulty starting to urinate and I need to go more often. It's really affecting my daily life.

[doctor] I can imagine that's quite inconvenient. Are there any other symptoms that you've noticed?

[patient] Yes, I've also been having some occasional lower back pain and I wake up twice every night to go to the bathroom.

[doctor] Okay, and how often do these symptoms occur?

[patient] Every day. It’s really causing a lot of interruptions, especially when I was still working as a teacher.

[doctor] That must be frustrating. Has it affected your sleep?

[patient] Yes, it has. I don’t sleep well because of the frequent trips to the bathroom at night.

[doctor] I understand. Do you have a balanced diet and do you exercise?

[patient] Yes, I try to eat healthy and avoid fatty foods. I also walk for about 30 minutes every day.

[doctor] That's good to hear. Do you smoke or drink alcohol?

[patient] I quit smoking 10 years ago. I used to smoke a pack a day for 15 years. I do drink 1-2 glasses of wine a week though.

[doctor] Okay, and any use of illicit drugs?

[patient] No, I don't use any drugs. I enjoy gardening and reading in my free time.

[doctor] Got it. Let’s go through some specific review of your systems. For genitourinary, you mentioned urinary hesitancy, frequency, and nocturia. Any other symptoms?

[patient] No, that’s about it.

[doctor] Okay. For musculoskeletal, you've mentioned occasional lower back pain. Is there anything else?

[patient] No, nothing else.

[doctor] And you’ve had poor sleep due to nocturia. Any general symptoms like fever, chills, or weight loss?

[patient] No, none of those.

[doctor] Alright, let’s move on to a quick physical exam. Your vitals are looking good: Blood pressure is 135/85 mmHg, heart rate is 74 bpm, temperature is 98.6°F, respiratory rate is 16 breaths/min, and oxygen saturation is 97% on room air.

[patient] That sounds normal, right?

[doctor] Yes, those are within normal ranges. Now, let me check your abdomen. It feels soft and non-tender, no organomegaly. Next, I’ll do a Digital Rectal Exam. This might be a bit uncomfortable.

[patient] Okay, I understand.

[doctor] Your prostate feels firm and irregular with some nodules. That’s concerning. Let me listen to your heart and lungs next. Your heart has a regular rate and rhythm, no murmurs. Your lungs are clear to auscultation bilaterally.

[patient] Is everything alright?

[doctor] No focal neurological deficits, which is good. I’m going to review and order some tests to get a clearer picture. We’re awaiting results from your PSA test and we’ll schedule a Pelvic MRI to evaluate the local extent of the disease.

[patient] What do you think it could be?

[doctor] Based on your exam and symptoms, it’s likely a malignant neoplasm of the prostate. We need to confirm with the tests.

[patient] Oh, that’s scary. What’s the next step?

[doctor] We’ll start hormone therapy with Leuprolide Acetate 22.5 mg, an IM injection once every 3 months. We’ll also order a PSA test now and then every 3 months to monitor your levels.

[patient] What about further treatment?

[doctor] I’ll refer you to an Oncologist for further management and to consider radiation therapy. We need to follow up in 3 months to assess your response to the hormone therapy.

[patient] What should I do in the meantime?

[doctor] We discussed your diagnosis and treatment options. It’s important to adhere to hormone therapy. Monitor for any new or worsening symptoms and report them promptly. Continue your healthy lifestyle with regular exercise and a balanced diet.

[patient] Okay, and when do I come back?

[doctor] Return to the clinic in 3 months for a follow-up. Ensure your PSA test is done before the next visit and schedule the Pelvic MRI as soon as possible.

[patient] Alright, I’ll do that.

[doctor] Do you have any other questions or concerns?

[patient] No, I think that covers everything for now.

[doctor] Great. We’ll keep a close eye on your condition and make sure you get the best care possible. Thank you for coming in today.

[patient] Thank you, doctor. I appreciate it.
